overview: Two of the three classic mechanisms of horizontal gene transfer in bacteria, distinguished by whether direct cell-to-cell contact is required.
genZNote: Transformation: DNA just floating by, picked up off the street. Conjugation: DNA handed over in person.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Uptake of naked, free extracellular DNA from the environment by a competent bacterial cell.
aspects.valueB: Direct transfer of DNA (typically a plasmid) from a donor to a recipient bacterium through a physical connection (sex pilus).

aspects.label: Mechanism of Transfer
aspects.valueA: Naked DNA crosses the cell envelope of a naturally or artificially competent cell.
aspects.valueB: DNA passes through a conjugation (mating) bridge formed by an F-pilus.

aspects.label: Cell-to-Cell Contact
aspects.valueA: Not required — DNA is acquired directly from the environment.
aspects.valueB: Required — donor and recipient cells must physically connect.

aspects.label: DNA Source
aspects.valueA: Free DNA released by lysed cells or added experimentally (e.g. in cloning).
aspects.valueB: A conjugative plasmid (e.g. F plasmid) or, rarely, chromosomal DNA mobilized by a plasmid, from a living donor cell.

aspects.label: Natural Examples
aspects.valueA: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria species undergo natural transformation.
aspects.valueB: F+ x F- mating in E. coli; a major route for spreading antibiotic resistance plasmids.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Uptake of free environmental DNA, no contact needed.
aspects.valueB: Direct DNA transfer via physical pilus connection between cells.
